items.rule: Shuffle all cards (goods cards and action cards together) to form a single common draw pile in the center of the table.
Deal 5 cards to each player, kept secret in hand.
Leave free space in front of each player where their sale piles will accumulate.
The youngest player starts.
On your turn you chain two or three simple actions chosen among: draw, lay down, sell.
Draw: take one card from the central draw pile to add to your hand.
Lay down: place one or more cards of the same type in front of you to start or add to a pile.
Sell: choose one of your piles, turn it face down into your score area, and gain the points corresponding to it.
Action cards can be drawn during the game and let a player steal a card from a neighbor, force someone to sell immediately, or swap hands with another player.
An opponent playing an action card against you can make you lose a pile, so waiting to sell is risky.
The game ends as soon as the draw pile is empty and nobody can draw any more.
Points come only from sold piles; each pile is worth points according to the number of identical cards in it at the time of sale.
A pile of 1 card is worth 1 point.
A pile of 2 cards is worth 3 points.
A pile of 3 cards is worth 6 points.
A pile of 4 cards is worth 10 points.
A pile of 5 or more cards is worth 15 points.
Cards remaining in hand at the end of the game (and unsold piles) score nothing.
The player with the highest total of points from sold piles wins.
In case of a tie, the tied player with the fewest cards left in hand wins.
